description:
Hi! 

We will work on creating a health monitoring software to make astronauts able to easily assess, store and review their health stats.
summary:
ASTER: health intelligence for long-duration spaceflight.
Radiation, isolation, altered gravity and a hostile closed environment can change an astronaut's immune system, bones, heart and mental health. Far from Earth, the crew must spot these changes themselves. ASTER gives the station crew and the ground medical team two linked nodes that share one health record. It collects health indicators, checks the data, compares new measurements with each astronaut's past results, and organizes them into groups. Charts, tables and a schedule of past and upcoming tests show how health changes over time. An AI assistant, limited to calculated facts, explains the history and flags slow drift early for both astronauts and doctors. Doctors review the data and give advice and an action plan. Astronauts confirm the results, which are saved and used in the next monitoring cycle.
details:
What It Does and How It Works

- ASTER is a web application that tracks astronaut health during space missions. It runs as two nodes: a station crew node and a ground medical node. Both read and write the same record, so the crew and the doctors always see the same numbers.
- Users must first select a mission and a crew member before any data loads. This stops health records from getting mixed up.
- The app tracks body metrics (such as heart rate, blood pressure, body temperature and sleep) and cabin air readings (such as oxygen and carbon dioxide levels), and many more can be added. It calculates each crew member's baseline values and daily changes and shows them as graphs over time, so slow changes are easy to see. Bad or missing sensor readings are highlighted in red and never hidden or smoothed out.
- A schedule shows past and upcoming medical tests and appointments, alongside the measurements taken. A built-in AI assistant uses this history, the schedule and the crew's notes to answer questions about the numbers and give context. It is instructed never to give medical diagnoses. All notes and conversations are logged.
- The application is modular. Sensors and test results are added through plugins. Images, video, files and text notes can also be added, and the AI helps interpret them when no specialist analysis software is available.
- Planned: a local AI model so health data stays on board, logins and user roles to protect confidentiality, and trajectory-aware synchronization that plans around communication delay.


Benefits and Impact
- Far from Earth, radio signals take time: up to about 22 minutes each way to Mars. Astronauts cannot always wait for doctors on Earth to answer basic questions. ASTER lets the crew check their own health trends immediately, while the ground medical team sees the same record, reviews it, and gives advice and an action plan.
- The system does all the math first and gives the AI only the final calculated numbers, with references to where they came from. This reduces the chance of the AI inventing data, although its summaries still need review by a doctor. Together with the trend charts, this helps astronauts spot physical changes early while staying safe.
- All conversations and notes are logged and accessible if needed. To protect privacy, the AI will run a local model in the future, and logins and user roles are planned.

Tools and Technologies

- Coding Languages: TypeScript, HTML, and CSS.
- Frameworks and Libraries: React and TanStack Start for the web framework, Tailwind - CSS for styling, and Recharts for the line charts.
- Testing: Vitest to test the math and page routing.

- AI Service: A cloud language model that runs only on the server (a local model is planned).


Creative Approach and Key Factors

- Two Nodes, One Record: The crew and the ground medical team each have their own node over one shared record, so both see the same data.

- AI Safety: The AI is instructed to use only calculated facts and to point to where the data came from. It does not give diagnoses, and its drafts need doctor review.

- Context-Aware AI: The AI sees the schedule of past and upcoming tests as well as the measurements, so its explanations fit what is happening and what comes next.

- Air and Body Data Together: The app shows cabin air quality (and other environmental factors in the future) alongside crew vitals, making it easy to see if bad air is causing physical symptoms.

- Data Honesty: Missing or poor sensor readings are clearly shown rather than hidden or smoothed out.

- Flexible Code: The data, the math, and the screens are kept in separate files so real spacecraft sensors can be added through plugins.

- Planned, Built for Delay: Trajectory-aware synchronization will let the nodes plan around communication delay as a spacecraft travels farther from Earth.
